The box-by-box companion

A private, offline guide to the 35-slide presentation: exact slide wording, plain-language explanations and what to say aloud.

Core result: commanded jump 20/20 nominal; best imitation row completed 20/20 clips, but full L1 stayed 0/20.

Terms I may need to explain
L1The full reference-tracking success contract: complete without a fall/non-foot contact, sufficient physical flight, enough recovery speed, and joint-angle error within both limits. A row needs at least 16/20 full passes.c2 / c3Two separate repaired motion references. Original c2 uses a 0.24 s flight gate; c3 variant uses its separately anchored 0.32 s gate.RMSRoot mean square joint-angle error, in radians. It measures mismatch over 24 joints; lower is better, but a lower early-terminated average is not proof of full-clip tracking.Body weight (BW)Landing contact force normalized by the mass and gravity in the specific simulated robot model. It is not an injury or hardware-safety rating.Action delayA delay in applying the motor position target in the simulation. This is different from delayed observations or real network timing.SeedA reproducibility setting. Twenty evaluation seeds vary rollouts from one trained checkpoint; they are not twenty independent trained policies.Box-by-boxThe left side quotes each PowerPoint text box exactly. The right side explains its meaning and limits. Figures get their own explanations.VideoNo new rendered rollout video exists for this sweep. This artifact deliberately presents real numeric charts, not an unrelated old video.

All images and explanations are embedded. No network, account or external library is needed. Private LAFAN-derived media and models are not included.

The project goal is a reusable bag of R1 movement skills

Box by box · exact PowerPoint wording
What is on the slideWhat it means
The project goal is a reusable bag of R1 movement skills

Slide purpose: My long-term idea is a bag of skills that I can use in one simulated scene. The R1 should follow movement commands and perform actions while staying balanced. That makes transitions important: I need to know not only whether it can jump, but whether it can run into the jump and keep moving afterward. Nothing in this presentation is a physical-robot demonstration.

A skill should be controllable and connect to the next skill.

Scope and setup for this slide. My long-term idea is a bag of skills that I can use in one simulated scene. The R1 should follow movement commands and perform actions while staying balanced. That makes transitions important: I need to know not only whether it can jump, but whether it can run into the jump and keep moving afterward. Nothing in this presentation is a physical-robot demonstration.

Robot and environment

MuJoCo computes contact, gravity and movement. The actor must balance the body by commanding joints; this is not a prerecorded animation.

Unitree R1 humanoid, modeled in MuJoCo physics.

MuJoCo computes contact, gravity and movement. The actor must balance the body by commanding joints; this is not a prerecorded animation.

Long-term use

The skill-bag idea is to combine reusable behaviors for an interactive game or scene rather than train one long fixed performance.

Move through a simulated scene: stand, walk, run, jump and perform actions.

The skill-bag idea is to combine reusable behaviors for an interactive game or scene rather than train one long fixed performance.

Why connections matter

A good-looking jump is insufficient if the robot falls after landing or cannot resume locomotion.

A policy must recover into a usable state for the next action.

A good-looking jump is insufficient if the robot falls after landing or cannot resume locomotion.

Slide purpose: Week 31 had three parts. First, I trained a speed-command locomotion policy. Second, I obtained a jumping-jacks tracker through the human-video pipeline. These were useful starting points, not the completed Week 32 milestone.

SLIDE 05 / 35

Week 31 left three specific gaps

Box by box · exact PowerPoint wording
What is on the slideWhat it means
Week 31 left three specific gaps

Slide purpose: The important distinction is between the names of the skills and the measured behavior. A policy going fast can still be walking. Jumping jacks can leave the ground without solving a running jump. And one successful rollout does not tell me how the skill handles different timing or delays. Those were the gaps I turned into explicit tests.

These gaps explain the experiment order in Week 32.

Scope and setup for this slide. The important distinction is between the names of the skills and the measured behavior. A policy going fast can still be walking. Jumping jacks can leave the ground without solving a running jump. And one successful rollout does not tell me how the skill handles different timing or delays. Those were the gaps I turned into explicit tests.

Fast walk ≠ true run

The later running test requires repeated brief flight phases and alternating support, not just a high commanded speed.

Speed alone did not establish a running gait.

The later running test requires repeated brief flight phases and alternating support, not just a high commanded speed.

Jumping jacks ≠ running jump

A continuous running jump needs the skills to work while the body is already moving and after the landing.

A jump in place did not establish approach, forward travel and recovery.

A continuous running jump needs the skills to work while the body is already moving and after the landing.

Working once ≠ reliable skill

Repeated seeded evaluations, disturbed conditions and defined failure criteria are needed before a stronger claim.

Delay and difficult transitions could break a policy.

Repeated seeded evaluations, disturbed conditions and defined failure criteria are needed before a stronger claim.

SLIDE 08 / 35

Four terms make the rest of the talk easier to follow

Box by box · exact PowerPoint wording
What is on the slideWhat it means
Four terms make the rest of the talk easier to follow

Slide purpose: A policy is the actual learned controller. A reference is a target motion. Training changes the controller to pursue its rewards or reference, while evaluation freezes the controller and applies a fixed test. This is why I separate the learning curves from the final success counts. The terms are related but not interchangeable.

A learned controller is different from the motion it is trying to follow.

Scope and setup for this slide. A policy is the actual learned controller. A reference is a target motion. Training changes the controller to pursue its rewards or reference, while evaluation freezes the controller and applies a fixed test. This is why I separate the learning curves from the final success counts. The terms are related but not interchangeable.

Policy

The policy runs repeatedly while physics advances; it must react to the body state, not merely play recorded joint angles.

The trained controller: robot observations in, joint commands out.

The policy runs repeatedly while physics advances; it must react to the body state, not merely play recorded joint angles.

Reference

A reference tells the tracker where the body and joints should be over time. It is a target, not proof that a robot can physically execute it.

A desired motion trajectory, expressed for the R1 body.

A reference tells the tracker where the body and joints should be over time. It is a target, not proof that a robot can physically execute it.

Training versus evaluation

A reward is a numerical training incentive. An evaluation gate is a fixed success requirement; a high reward or long episode does not override a failed gate.

Training updates the policy; evaluation freezes it and measures behavior.

A reward is a numerical training incentive. An evaluation gate is a fixed success requirement; a high reward or long episode does not override a failed gate.

Scope and setup for this slide. This is a step missing from my earlier summary. I did not jump directly from Week 31’s fast walk to the final jump result. What I changed

The parent was the Week 31 speed-command policy, not a new human-motion tracker. A second fine-tune increased foot-clearance margin.

I adjusted the running gait schedule and rewarded real flight at faster commands.

What the running test required

Both feet must be off the ground under force-and-height checks. Short windows throughout the run must satisfy the gait requirements.

Forward speed, repeated flight phases, alternating steps and no fall.

I found that its reward measured pelvis rise from the time of the request, while the test measured whole-body rise after takeoff. Those are different quantities. I changed the reward definition and weight, trained further and reported the fixed final checkpoint. It passed twenty of twenty nominal trials, but the stronger jump also made landing forces larger.

I aligned the training reward with the height measured by the test.

SLIDE 20 / 35

A complete imitation pass required four things together

Box by box · exact PowerPoint wording
What is on the slideWhat it means
A complete imitation pass required four things together

Slide purpose: The logs call this the L1 gate. I use full test in the slides. It is a conjunction: finishing without a fall or unintended body contact, enough physical flight, adequate recovery speed, and sufficiently accurate joint tracking. For the original c2 reference, physical flight must last at least 0.24 seconds. Mean joint RMS must stay at or below 0.15 radians, roughly nine degrees, with the higher-percentile bound also met. A row needs sixteen full passes out of twenty. The command route uses a different test, so its 0.12-second jump threshold must not be substituted here.

At least 16 of 20 episodes must pass every requirement, not merely finish the clip.

Scope and setup for this slide. The logs call this the L1 gate. I use full test in the slides. It is a conjunction: finishing without a fall or unintended body contact, enough physical flight, adequate recovery speed, and sufficiently accurate joint tracking. For the original c2 reference, physical flight must last at least 0.24 seconds. Mean joint RMS must stay at or below 0.15 radians, roughly nine degrees, with the higher-percentile bound also met. A row needs sixteen full passes out of twenty. The command route uses a different test, so its 0.12-second jump threshold must not be substituted here.

1 · Complete without a fall

The no-fall gate combines completion with no non-foot contact. A policy can finish the clip but still fail this gate.

Follow the full reference and avoid unintended body contact.

The no-fall gate combines completion with no non-foot contact. A policy can finish the clip but still fail this gate.

2 · Flight and recovery

Original c2 requires at least 0.24 seconds of physical flight and recovery to about 2.31 m/s in the defined post-landing window.

Meet the required airborne duration, then regain forward speed.

Original c2 requires at least 0.24 seconds of physical flight and recovery to about 2.31 m/s in the defined post-landing window.

3 · Track the joint motion

The mean RMS limit is 0.15 radians, about 9 degrees; the 95th-percentile limit is 0.30 radians, about 17 degrees. These measure joint mismatch, not a fall.

Keep mean and peak-percentile joint errors within the fixed limits.

The mean RMS limit is 0.15 radians, about 9 degrees; the 95th-percentile limit is 0.30 radians, about 17 degrees. These measure joint mismatch, not a fall.
